html:
SMTO-LLM-0057 — That model server action isn't available on this Gateway

GUID: 43fedb1f-2a24-5ebf-8133-c7ed21114755
Slug: local-ai-capability-unavailable
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't do this model server action with the chosen program or on that computer, or another model server job was still busy there.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to show the Local AI status for that Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer, and check whether a model server from earlier is already running. SMTO only runs one heavy model server job at a time per Gateway, and the status lists which actions each program supports there.
  2. If your profile uses LM Studio or a generic OpenAI-compatible server, start or stop that server yourself; SMTO can only check those. SMTO doesn't control those programs, so start, stop and restart aren't offered for them.
  3. If you added extra options or an API key to the profile in Parameter Store, remove the ones the installed program doesn't support, then select Save. SMTO refuses to pass options the installed model server program doesn't list as supported.
  4. When nothing else is running, ask again in a new message. A new message uses the saved profile and a free Gateway.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the action finished, and the Local AI status shows the expected result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't stop model server programs on that computer that SMTO didn't start, and don't repeat an action whose result you haven't checked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested Local AI operation is not supported for this provider or host, or not admitted right now: Windows Gateway, an external-only provider (LM Studio, generic OpenAI-compatible), a profile option or API key the installed executable does not advertise, an Ollama managed launch with a key, a busy heavy-operation slot, or the runtime record limit.

What this means

  • The requested management feature is unsupported or unavailable under the adapter, platform or bounded admission state; a missing activation service can also produce this category. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The requested management feature is unsupported or unavailable under the adapter, platform or bounded admission state; a missing activation service can also produce this category.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare advertised features and current admission/runtime counts; distinguish unsupported lifecycle management from temporary capacity exhaustion.

How to fix it

  • Check local_ai.status for the provider's advertised features on that Gateway. Remove profile options or api_key_ref the installed executable's --help does not list, manage LM Studio/generic endpoints outside SMTO, use a Linux/macOS Gateway for managed lifecycle, or wait for an in-flight start/restart/pull/remove to settle. Do not bypass ownership checks.
  • Choose a supported operation/provider or wait for occupied admission capacity to settle; do not bypass lifecycle ownership checks.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected operation is advertised and admitted on the intended Gateway.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
